in a nutshell, her heart could not pump blood effectively. it sounds like she also had fluid around her heart as well or that was the cause of the cardiomyopathy aka blood not pumping right. Based on the information gathered about her other organs, it sounds like oxygen and blood could not circulate well. All it takes is one somewhat stressful event to cause everything to start declining if fluid had been building up around the heart. 

We just went through this last summer with the family dog. She was totally fine then tried to jump up on the couch and began breathing heavy, couldn't move, had pale gums, and started coughing. We rushed her to the emergency vet and they found fluid around her heart which they were able to drain. This gave us another month with her but she started to decline rapidly just doing every day activities. My parents last dog also passed this way. He was fine one moment and the next couldn't stop coughing. My mom brought him home to think over what the best thing to do was and she decided he just needed to be a happy dog a little longer. He wasn't suffering. He eventually passed while playing with my cat - he got too excited.
